question.problem: A thin plate $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{4}{{y}^{2}}$ is enclosed between the curve $y={e}^{x}$ and the line $y=e$ for $0\le x\le 1.$ Find the moment of the plate about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is a type I plane region, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121640/assets/268322576d74a9d63d05e06f55011796e17c2b4ea7a96f583270b5c1cbdb14fb.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{e}^{x}\le y\le e}
$$

and $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{4}{{y}^{2}}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot \frac{4}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{4}{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{e}^{x}}^{e}\frac{4}{y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4[\operatorname{ln}⁡y]_{y={e}^{x}}^{y=e}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4(1-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4-4x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[4x-2{x}^{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =4-2-0 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$
